record.paper_title: Problèmes ouverts en théorie des intersections
record.original_question: Let G be a semi-simple simply connected algebraic group over the complex numbers and consider the natural homomorphism from the Chow ring A(G) to the integral cohomology H^*(G(C),Z) of the associated compact complex manifold. Is this homomorphism injective? More generally, when G has torsion, does this map detect the positive-degree part of A(G) in the way suggested by the comparison with torsion primes of G(C)?

evidence.quote: Il est tentant de conjecturer que l'homomorphisme (4.10) est en fait injectif, puisqu'on sait par ailleurs que les nombres premiers de torsion pour G(C) sont exactement ceux qui divisent l'ordre du groupe fini A^+(G).
On peut du moins affirmer que dans le cas du groupe G = G_2 sur le corps C, l'homomorphisme (4.10) n'est pas nul en degré > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a semi-simple, simply connected linear algebraic group over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$, and let $G(\mathbb{C})$ denote its associated compact (real) Lie group (equivalently, the underlying complex manifold endowed with its classical topology). Let $A(G) = \bigoplus_{i\ge 0} A^i(G)$ denote the Chow ring of $G$ (the ring of algebraic cycles on $G$ modulo rational equivalence), and let $H^{*}(G(\mathbb{C}), \mathbb{Z})$ denote its integral singular cohomology ring. There is a natural cycle-class ring homomorphism
$$ \mathrm{cl} : A(G) \longrightarrow H^{*}(G(\mathbb{C}), \mathbb{Z}), $$
which doubles degrees ($A^i(G) \to H^{2i}(G(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Z})$).

(1) Is the homomorphism $\mathrm{cl}$ injective for every such $G$?

(2) More precisely, let $A^{+}(G) = \bigoplus_{i>0} A^i(G)$. It is known that the torsion primes of $G(\mathbb{C})$ (the primes $p$ for which $H^{*}(G(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Z})$ has $p$-torsion) are exactly the primes dividing the order of the finite group $A^{+}(G)$. Does the cycle map $\mathrm{cl}$ in fact detect $A^{+}(G)$ in a manner compatible with this coincidence of torsion primes — for instance, is $\mathrm{cl}$ restricted to $A^{+}(G)$ injective?

As a known partial fact one may use: for $G = G_2$ over $\mathbb{C}$, the cycle map $\mathrm{cl}$ is non-zero in positive degrees.
artifact.status_search_result: A direct affirmative or negative resolution of the injectivity of the cycle class map $A(G)\to H^{*}(G(\mathbb{C}),\mathbb{Z})$ for all semi-simple simply connected complex algebraic groups was not located. Related work (Totaro, Pandharipande, Yagita, Gu, and others) computes Chow rings of classifying spaces $BG$ and exceptional groups and shows interesting torsion phenomena, but a definitive published statement settling the conjecture for $G$ itself in full generality could not be confirmed from the search.

status_evidence.title: The Chow Ring of a Classifying Space (Totaro)
status_evidence.snippet: Computes Chow rings of classifying spaces of algebraic groups and compares them to integral cohomology, exhibiting both agreements and torsion phenomena.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational work on cycle maps from Chow rings of (classifying spaces of) algebraic groups to integral cohomology; injectivity questions remain delicate.

status_evidence.title: Some torsion classes in the Chow ring and cohomology of BPGLn (Gu, 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs explicit torsion classes in Chow and cohomology of classifying spaces of projective linear groups.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on the comparison of Chow and cohomology for algebraic groups continues, indicating the precise injectivity question is not closed.
